note: A grappler's card at the top: Allen's five-round top game against Duncan's untested cardio, Camilo's wrestling against a 38-year-old striker, and Godínez's volume against a clincher. Two overrides of the model, both for things it can't see: Allen over five rounds, and Prado against a short-notice opponent on a three-fight skid. The finishes I pick are all first-round reads, where the winner's own record and the loser's finishes line up.

picks.bout: Brendan Allen vs Christian Leroy Duncan
picks.why: Override: the model leans Duncan on striking, but five rounds favour Allen's grinding top game against a fighter who has never gone past round three; the market agrees. Duncan has never been submitted, so the cards over a tap.
A 25-year-old wrestler out-working a 38-year-old range striker; Herbert's power keeps it honest, so I take the model's decision rather than a finish.
Godínez's volume and takedowns against a striker who drifts into clinches; her losses are only to elite grapplers. She wins rounds rather than finishing: decision.

picks.bout: Andre Fili vs Kai Kamaka III
picks.why: Following the model on Kamaka's accuracy and volume, though the market and my small read lean Fili; close to a coin flip. A decision, as most of Fili's fights are.
